clue.text: 16 across's key broadcast

definitions.note: 16 across is a light in this grid meaning a heavenly body, and the 's stands for 'is'

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Someone explains which key a song by a celebrity was broadcast in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the answer to 16 across, a celestial body; ALT is the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest point of light in the constellation Aquila, one of the best-known in the night sky.

clue.text: A very bad chap in good heart, a shade of green

indicators.note: the bad chap sits inside the middle letters
the middle two letters of good

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A villain with a good heart, oddly coloured green.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a dull yellowish-green colour named after the fruit's skin and flesh.

clue.text: Chip that's passed quality control eaten by round figure

indicators.note: the approval is swallowed by the number

parts.note: ten is a round number
OK means approved, passed as fine

explanation.surface: A potato chip that passed inspection is eaten by a portly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round figure' suggests a plump person; it is a round number.
explanation.definitionFit: A token or chip is a counter used in place of money, as at a casino.

clue.text: Test of personality I note well, consuming king a good deal

indicators.note: the abbreviation swallows the king's letter

parts.note: NB is nota bene, Latin for note well
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a lot means a large amount

explanation.surface: A personality test where a monarch eats a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rorschach test asks people what they see in ink-blot patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rorschach inkblot test is a psychological test interpreting how people read blot shapes.

clue.text: Describing lavish meal, drink with drink to drink

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it in, so one drink word swallows the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A boozy feast description: drink after drink after drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the joke: two drinks are pieces, and the third, with 'to', is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a British colloquial term for a large, extravagant feast.

clue.text: Spot company cutting Israeli fliers up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole is read from the bottom
the company cuts into the airline's name

parts.note: El Al is Israel's national airline

explanation.surface: A firm spotted interrupting Israeli pilots as they take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' makes ELACOL, which 'up' turns round, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is a place or setting, a spot where something happens.

clue.text: One's recognised in this clue by Paul, only the first, that is — it's rubbish!

indicators.note: rubbish is a mess, so the letters are thrown into new order
only the opening letter of the setter's name is used

parts.note: i.e. is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Paul, the setter, mocks his own clue as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link before the anagram signal 'rubbish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in the public eye is famous and widely recognised by the general public.

clue.text: Church leader bound to punch head

indicators.note: the border word punches into the head word

parts.note: pate is an old word for head
a rim is a boundary or edge

explanation.surface: A clergyman is set to hit someone on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' looks like 'certain to'; 'bound' is RIM and 'to punch' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the chief bishop of a province.

clue.text: Notices penny, then pound astronomical

indicators.note: to pound something is to beat it into new shape

explanation.surface: Announcements of a penny, then astronomical pound prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests money after 'penny'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Proclamations are public announcements, formal notices issued by authority.

clue.text: One's hard to sway

definitions.meaning: a stone or boulder is something hard
to move gently from side to side

explanation.definitionFit: A rock is a hard mineral mass, and to rock is to move to and fro; it is also the music theme here.

clue.text: 9 16 across tuned back in with tour

indicators.note: tuning adjusts an instrument, so the letters are reset into new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician tunes up back on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 and 16 across combine to give 'rock star'; the answer was the Nirvana frontman.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Cobain fronted Nirvana and was one of the most famous rock musicians of the 1990s.

clue.text: Such bodily desires run through old trade route

indicators.note: one letter is placed running through the middle of the waterway

parts.note: a canal was a route for carrying goods by barge
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Lusty urges are said to have followed an ancient trading path.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal desires are physical, fleshly appetites, as opposed to spiritual ones.

clue.text: 9 required to kill one, old lady

definitions.note: light 9 is a slang word for a diamond

parts.note: to cull is to kill selectively
I is the Roman numeral one
nan is a British word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A gem is needed to murder a granny.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 9 means 'rock' in its slang sense of a diamond, not rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cullinan is the largest gem-quality diamond ever found, cut for the British Crown Jewels.

clue.text: Milk on order sent back, some rejected cheese

indicators.note: the milk word is placed after the reversed order
the abbreviation for the honour is turned to read the other way

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
to milk is to exploit, to use

indicators.note: rejecting turns the word for some backwards

parts.note: part means some

explanation.surface: A diner sends back milk and refuses cheese in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' looks like dairy alongside 'cheese', but it means exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap was a British slang name for cheap, low-quality cheese, the sort used to bait traps.

clue.text: Earth's destroyer more alarming, if accepted

indicators.note: the comparative word takes in the two letters as if receiving them

parts.note: scarier means more frightening
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doomsday threat to the planet, if believed, is more frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' is soil, not the planet: the apocalyptic surface hides a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarifier is a tool that breaks up and loosens soil or lawn surfaces.

clue.text: Kiss 9 16 across — fancy immense snog?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a rock star's kiss is a fancy huge snog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss' is the band, not a smooch; the snog surface plays on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Simmons is the bassist and co-lead singer of the rock band Kiss.

clue.text: Bending over, I'm upset to see the principal

indicators.note: something bent over is turned back on itself, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: Rats! is an exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone bends over, upset, to meet the head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a show is its leading performer, the principal player.

clue.text: See 15
Rope binding female, S&M back for the holiday periods

indicators.note: the rope ties round the letter for female

parts.note: a halter is a rope used to lead a horse

indicators.note: the two letters are taken in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters S and M

explanation.surface: A kinky scene with rope and bondage, offered as half-term fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-terms are short school breaks in the middle of each British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-terms are week-long school breaks in the middle of each British term.

clue.text: Strong bloody item cast metal for 9 16 across

parts.note: F is forte, the musical mark for loud and strong
something bloody is red
a die is the item cast in a game of dice
mercury is a liquid metal

explanation.surface: A powerful, gory cast metal object is made for a rock star.
explanation.definitionFit: Freddie Mercury was the flamboyant lead singer of the rock band Queen.

clue.text: See 18
One seen in the distance, posh environment

indicators.note: the single letter is spotted inside the measure of distance

parts.note: a mile is a distance
I is the Roman numeral one
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: Someone glimpsed far off in an upmarket setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a social setting or surroundings.

clue.text: Male in club with three individuals, drunk, showing navels

indicators.note: being drunk leaves things in a jumble, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
III is three single units, Roman numeral ones

explanation.surface: A man in a nightclub with three others, drunk, flashing their bellies.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbilici is the Latin plural of umbilicus, the belly button.

clue.text: Naughty youngsters going topless to show boobs

indicators.note: the first letter, the word's top, is removed

parts.note: little terrors are badly behaved children

explanation.surface: Badly behaved kids strip their tops to flash their chests.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a slang word for a blunder or mistake.

clue.text: 16 across US state getting set

definitions.note: a light of this grid meaning a heavenly body

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A US celebrity's state is getting settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigel is the brightest point of light in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Set to put bottom on top of items, one packing case

indicators.note: the case is packed with the other pieces

parts.note: a pod is a seed case

indicators.note: the first letter goes after the word for sitting

parts.note: to sit is to put one's bottom down

indicators.note: the first letter of the word items

explanation.surface: Instructions for loading a packing case with each item's bottom on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' has the seed case wrap round the rest, splitting after its second letter; 'items' looks like the packed goods but gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set in place has been positioned, put deliberately in a spot.

clue.text: Dirty wipes by food

indicators.note: wiping removes, so the two-letter word is erased from the longer word

parts.note: grubby means dirty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with grimy wipes reaches for a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for food.

clue.text: Initiation of screen goddess captivates you, seeing 16 across

indicators.note: the beginning letter of screen
to captivate is to hold, so the goddess holds the letter

parts.note: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A film goddess's debut wins over a viewer looking at a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest point of light in the night sky.

clue.text: Very petite derrière taken in series of shots

indicators.note: the long exchange takes the single letter inside it

parts.note: a rally is a long exchange of shots in tennis

indicators.note: a derrière is a backside, so the last letter of petite

explanation.surface: A petite bottom captured in a sequence of photos.
explanation.definitionFit: Really, as in really good, is an intensifier meaning very.
